scope: 16 existing source text files covering 11 states; source provenance and version audit, not the complete ADR 0014 agreement-requirements walk.
currency_meaning: Limited to identified pages/versions inspected on the recorded retrieval date. An official historical match or a current index link is not proof that all later amendments or implementing authorities were found.

extraction.pdf: pdftotext reading order or -layout as specified per comparison
extraction.html: Python HTMLParser; scripts/styles/noscript excluded; block line breaks; HTML entities decoded; horizontal whitespace normalized.
extraction.comparison_hashes: SHA-256 of UTF-8 normalized selected body, no trailing newline; collapse-whitespace means Python split/join, remove-whitespace removes only whitespace. Publication line-number removal is described in README; substantive numeric tokens are retained.
extraction.raw_responses: Only the two PDFs listed under archived_response are duplicated here. Other retrieved response hashes identify the downloads inspected, not permanent availability at mutable URLs. Selected text evidence is retained separately.

comparison.excluded_prefix: Publisher: California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation Site: https://dfpi.ca.gov Recorded: 2026-09-08 10 CCR §§900-956 — the DFPI rulemaking adopting Subchapter 3, Commercial Financing Disclosures. The file opens with the Department's own adoption language: "The Department of Financial Protection and Innovation hereby adopts the following new provisions to be added to Title 10, Chapter 3". WHY THIS HEADER SAYS "PUBLISHER" AND NOT "RETRIEVED FROM". The deep link this file was fetched through was not written down at the time and is not recoverable — the Kansas and California paths tried on 2026-09-08 now 301 into 404s, because legislatures reorganise their sites. What IS determinable, from the document itself, is who published it: an enrolled act, a chamber's letterhead and a Superintendent's signed adoption are not things a reproducer manufactures. So this records the publisher and the publisher's site, dated today, as a statement about what the document IS. It is deliberately not a claim that these bytes were served from that host on that date — only a fetch recorded at the moment of fetching can say that, which is what `CT-CGS-36a-861-872.txt` and `VA-Code-6.2-2228-2238.txt` have and these do not. THE DIGEST MOVED AND THE VERIFICATION DATE DID NOT. Adding these lines changes the file, so its digest was recomputed. Not one byte of the statutory text changed — the same treatment, and the same reason, as the two headers added in `fix/ga-primary-text`: "the digest broke, I updated it" is the move this mechanism exists to make somebody justify, so the justification is written here. --- STATUTORY TEXT BEGINS ---

comparison.excluded_prefix: O.C.G.A. § 10-1-393.18 — REQUIRED DISCLOSURES FOR COMMERCIAL FINANCING TRANSACTIONS; EXCEPTIONS; LIMITATIONS ON BROKERS; ENFORCEMENT; CIVIL PENALTIES PRIMARY TEXT. Senate Bill 90, 2023-2024 regular session, AS PASSED (enrolled), published by the Georgia General Assembly at https://www.legis.ga.gov/api/legislation/document/20232024/219440 Retrieved 2026-09-07. Enacted Ga. L. 2023, p. 255, § 2/SB 90, effective January 1, 2024. This REPLACES a browser capture of law.justia.com, which was a secondary publisher and was incomplete: subsection (a)'s definitions and the full text of (b)-(k) were not in it, so "advance fee" -- a term the broker prohibition in (f)(1) turns on -- was defined nowhere in what we held, while the Georgia content spec nonetheless carried a verification date against it. The earlier note that "the Georgia legislature's document API returns an unrelated resolution" was a wrong document id, not a broken API. The enrolled bill is the act as passed. Where a later amendment changes the Code, this file is superseded and the digest will say so. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
